objective: Determine whether the existing trainable Cyclic-MGU architecture can correctly integrate its fixed cyclic ALU into the register-machine execution pipeline and generalize modular addition to the registered validation pairs.
hypothesis: The fixed cyclic arithmetic inductive bias may allow Cyclic-MGU to generalize modular addition more reliably than the tested Slot-MGU and Vanilla GRU configurations, provided that surrounding trainable components integrate the arithmetic result into execution.
scientific_distinction: The cyclic ALU is fixed and analytical. A successful result demonstrates integration of a deterministic arithmetic component into a trainable architecture, not learned arithmetic from data.
